newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bill to ban MMT reaches final stage.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bill to ban MMT reaches final stage.

text.p: The Canadian government's attempts to effectively ban MMT, a gasoline additive produced for Canada mainly by Ethyl Corp of Virginia, are about to come to a head.

The bill, which aims to prevent imports and interprovincial trade of methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, has already passed through the House of Commons and through the Senate's energy committee, despite Ethyl Corp's threat of a US$200 million legal case against it.
The controversial legislation now awaits a final vote in the unelected Senate, widely expected this week.

"I think the Canadian government, on behalf of Canadians, is certainly within its rights to pass this legislation for the protection of health and environmental concerns," Environment Minister told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday. "No threat will change that."
Ethyl Corp filed an intent to lay a claim under the North American Free Trade Agreement last September. Some of the provinces have also said they oppose the bill.
Asked if the Senate is likely to pass the bill, Marchi said "Yes, I think so."
But the passage of the bill is by no means certain.
